# Choosing the hook

The hook is the thing of everyday life the idea is tied to. It is the first thing drawn and the question the drawing
opens with.

A good hook:
- is something the audience has seen or done (a card bill, a bus stop, a café queue), not something they have to imagine;
- already holds the idea: taking it apart reveals the idea without forcing it;
- can be drawn with few shapes (a person, a house, a cart, a table);
- has a number in it only when the idea is about a number.

Offer up to three, best first, each with one line saying why it works for this audience. Avoid:
- hooks that need a fact the person may not know to make sense;
- hooks tied to one country, brand or person (unless the person asked);
- sad or delicate situations (illness, debt shame, accidents) unless the person brought them.
